In the back wall of the well contains the enshrined mummy of the first Rope Shrine Maiden. On the left side of the Moon Well there is a door that opens to the Hell Bridge, a path that leads to the Rope Altar. Kirie's Hairpin is used to unlock this doorway in a slot near the mummy.

The cabinet of the shrine acts as a trick mechanism that requires a routine to be performed. This routine required the symbols carried by the four priests participating in the ceremony to be placed on each of the four sides of the cabinet, and the Himuro Family Master's seal to be placed into the recess of the cabinet that faced the entrance. The cabinet would then move from its place to reveal a ladder as well as causing moonlight to shine down into the well.

This routine was to be performed before the Strangling Ritual. The Rope Shrine Maiden would descend the ladder into the well and purify herself in the moonlight, then unlock the door with the hairpin and then go through the doorway leading to the Hell Bridge. Only she was allowed to use this path, while the rest of the Himuro family only entered the path leading from the Demon Mouth.

entries.name: (Ghost) Blinded Woman
entries.content:
The Blinded Maiden is the hostile ghost of the last Blind Demon to perform the Demon Tag Ritual prior to the Calamity. She was one of a line of maidens chosen to perform the Blinding and Demon Tag Rituals of Himuro Mansion.

Blinded was a member of the Himuro family. Upon reaching the age of 7 years, 9 months and 25 days, she was obligated to take part in the Demon Tag Ritual, like the rest of the young girls of the Himuro family her age. Every 10 years the entire Himuro family was obligated to gather at Himuro Mansion to perform a set of rituals to seal the Hell Gate, as well as prepare for the next set of rituals that would occur 10 years later. One of the rituals performed was a game of Demon Tag. It served as a means to select the next Rope Shrine Maiden and Blind Demon for the next set of rituals. The first child to be caught became the next Blind Demon for the next game of Demon Tag. Blinded was chosen to be the next Blind Demon in the same game of Demon Tag that Kirie was chosen to become the next Rope Shrine Maiden.

It is unknown if, like Kirie, Blinded stayed at the mansion in seclusion or was allowed to live a normal life prior to the Blinding Ritual. When the appointed time came, she was led through the Hidden Passage to the Blinding Room, where she was held down from moving by the four Himuro Family Priests. The Himuro Family Master then approached with the ceremonial Blinding Mask and applied it to her face.

What happened to Blinded after this is not known, including if she was able to perform the Demon Tag Ceremony to choose the next Blinded Maiden and Rope Shrine Maiden. It is presumed she perished during the Calamity along with the other people killed.

After her death, Blinded's spirit returned to roam the mansion in search of the next Blind Demon. Miku encountered her spirit several times during her search for her missing brother. Once the curse over the mansion was broken by Miku, Blinded's spirit was able to rest in peace.

entries.name: (Location) Blinding Room
entries.content:
The Blinding Room is a room in Himuro Mansion. The Blinding Ritual was performed inside this room. The woman who was to become the Blinded Maiden was restrained as the Himuro Family Master placed the Blinding Mask over her eyes, thereby blinding her in preparation for the Demon Tag Ritual and Strangling Ritual.

The door to this room bears a strange, demonic mask. It is unlocked by hanging the Happy Mask, Sad Mask, Angry Mask and Joyful Mask on the pillar in the Mask Room.

entries.name: (Ritual) Blinding Ritual
entries.content:
The Blinding Ritual is a ritual performed before the Demon Tag Ritual in the Himuro Mansion. They used the Blinding Mask to create the Blinded Maiden or the 'oni' (demon). They used the blood of the maiden's eyes to weaken and "blind" the spirits of the Hell Gate. The maiden or the demon's duty is to choose in the Demon Tag Ritual the next Rope Shrine Maiden and Blinded Maiden to perform their respective rituals 10 years later.

⤳Preceding
A child is chosen to become the next Blinded Maiden via the Demon Tag Ritual. Of a group of girls playing the game, the first to become caught by the previous Blinded Maiden is chosen to become the next Blinded Maiden. The thinking behind this choice is either that the first caught by the "Demon" is the most oblivious to the supernatural, or spiritually "blind", or the most obvious and distracting to the supernatural, and therefore capable of drawing the Hell Gate's attention and focus, which negates as useless from the blinding.

The events and preparation between being chosen in the Demon Tag Ritual and fulfilling the Blinding Ritual are unknown. There is no mention found of the Blinded Maiden being held in seclusion or removed from her family, like the Rope Shrine Maiden. However, visions of the ritual and the ghost of the Blinded Maiden show the selected child grows at least to young adulthood before the ritual.

⤳The Ritual
On an unknown, appointed day prior to the next Strangling Ritual (December 13, every ten years), the selected new maiden is taken to the Blinding Room. She is then presented to the Ceremony Master who is wearing the Mask of Reflection, a mask which changes to reflect the wearer's soul. She is held by two, masked priests in a kneeling position in front of the Ceremony Master. The Ceremony Master then takes out the Blinding Mask from its storage location on the altar before forcing the mask down upon the maiden's face, blinding her with the spikes inside the mask's eyes.

⤳Result
The bloodied mask is removed from the Blind Maiden's face and inserted like a key for the doorway located in the Demon Mouth that opens a path that the Himuro Family took to enter the Rope Altar. The maiden's blood is said to 'blind' the spirits/demons beyond the Hell Gate and weaken them in preparation for the Strangling Ritual.

The Blinded Maiden also fills her duty as the "oni" of the next Demon Tag Ritual (November 26) , selecting the next Rope Shrine Maiden and the next Blind Demon.

It is not known what happens happens to the maiden between her blinding and the other rituals, or what happens to the Blinded Maiden after the mask is removed.

entries.name: (Term) Blinded Maiden
entries.content:
The Blinded Maiden is a woman who is chosen to perform the Blinding and Demon Tag Ritual.

The Blinded Maiden plays an integral role in the rituals of the Himuro Mansion, and is a counterpoint to the Rope Shrine Maiden.

Her main duties include:
1. Lending strength to the Blinding Mask, during the Blinding Ritual.
2. Choosing the next Rope Shrine Maiden and Blind Maiden during the Demon Tag Ritual.
3. Acting as a way to distract or blind the forces behind the Hell Gate.

entries.name: (Term) Kagome, Kagome
entries.content:
Kagome, Kagome (かごめかごめ) is a children's song game.

In order to play, a child who was the "it", in other words the "Demon" (Oni 鬼), would stand or sit with their eyes covered or blindfolded. The other children would form a circle around the "it" and then dance around the circle singing the song, then the "it" would have to guess which of the children is standing behind them. If the "it" guessed correctly, then the person behind them would be the new "Demon".

entries.name: (Ritual) Demon Tag
entries.content:
Demon Tag is used as the means of choosing the new Blinded Maiden and Rope Shrine Maiden.

⤳Preparation
Girls of the minimum age of 7 years, 9 months, and 25 days are gathered at the mansion into an undisclosed location to play the game. The game is held in the Demon Mouth room. The newly Blinded Maiden is also present wearing the Blinding Mask as a blindfold.

⤳The Ritual
The "demon" in the Demon Tag is the Blinded Maiden, who is wearing the Blinding Mask as a blindfold. During demon tag, the "it" or the "demon" chases and catches the others in a normal game of tag, though in this case, the demon (Blinded) cannot see. During Kagome Kagome a blindfolded "demon" is in the center as the other players circle around them, chanting a song. When the song ends, the demon must guess who is behind them based on who they heard singing.

At an undisclosed time prior to the Demon Tag Ritual, the girl chosen as the new Blinded Maiden undergoes the Blinding Ceremony, where her eyes are gouged out using the Blinding Mask. The Demon Tag ritual begins when all female children in the family of the appropriate age are gathered on November 26th, once every 10 years, presumably in the Demon Mouth room, to play the game with the new Blinded Maiden acting as "it" or the "demon". The game is played until all the participants are caught by the Blinded Maiden.

Roles are given to the girls that get caught by the Blinded Maiden in a specific order.

Blinded Maiden: The first girl caught is prepared to be the next Blinded Maiden in the next future Demon Tag Ritual. She is thought to have the worst spiritual powers, or to be "blind" to the demons of the Hell Mouth. Her literal and spiritual blindness are used to dull the demon's senses, making it safe to open the doors and enter the Hell Mouth, and prevent unintentional leaks. While the first girl caught becomes the next Blinded Maiden, it is unknown what happens to her immediately after the ritual, or in the time between the ritual and when she becomes the next Blinded.

Rope Shrine Maiden: The last girl caught is prepared to be the next Rope Shrine Maiden. She is thought to have the highest 'Holy Power' because she was able to evade the 'demon' (Blinded) for the longest time. The next Rope Shrine Maiden is removed from her family and kept in seclusion for the next 10 years, preparing her for the Strangling Ritual.

The fate of the Blinded Maiden after she fills her purpose in the Demon Tag Ritual is unknown. The Blinding Mask she wears must be removed from her face and used as a key to enter the Banned Path by December 13th when the Strangling Ritual is performed. What happens to the Blinded Maiden for the 18 days between the Demon Tag Ritual and the Strangling Ritual is unknown. It is also unknown if the Blinded Maiden is permitted to live, is sacrificed herself, or dies from the shock or blood loss caused by the Blinding Mask's removal, or how any of those scenarios may be carried out.

entries.name: (Item) Blinding Mask
entries.content:
The Blinding Mask was used in the Blinding Ritual. It had two stakes through the eye holes, designed to pierce the eyes of the wearer and blind them.

The maiden on which the ceremony was to be performed was chosen by a game of Demon Tag.

Approximately 10 years later, the maiden to participate in the ceremony was led to the Blinding Room. She was then restrained by two priests who held her eyes open. The mask was then pushed into the maiden's eyes by the Ceremony Master.

The mask is also used to unlock the huge doors in the Demon Mouth.

entries.name: (Ghost) Floating Woman
entries.content: Floating Woman is a hostile female spirit. Much like Wandering Man little is known about her, other than she was already dead before the Calamity happened and it gave her the ability to return to the land of the living, she now wanders Himuro Mansion, looking for living persons she can drag with her into the Land of the Dead.

entries.name: (Ghost) Floating Face
entries.content: Floating Face is a hostile male spirit. The only thing that is known about him is that he is an ancient spirit, he has been cursed by the Malice for such a long time that he has lost his form, and has been reduced to a face in a cloud of mist.

entries.name: (Ghost) Kirie Himuro
entries.content:
Setting:【Fatal Frame】
Name:【Kirie Himuro】
Species:【Ghost】
Gender:【Female】
Occupation:【Rope Shrine Maiden】
Physical Appearance:【Kirie is a ghost with a slim figure and pale skin. Kirie wears a stained white kimono, with the lacerations ropes used in her ritual still tied to her limbs. She is surrounded by a dark presence, the Malice, appearing as a throng of ghostly bodies congealed into one. Kirie's eyes are never shown, being hidden by her long black hair, and she moves through the air, her feet never touching the ground.】
Personality:【Kirie was a previously youthful girl, accepting of her fate and glad to serve her family in the sacrifice. However, once she met her lover, she became hopeful of life, something that Lord Himuro and his followers could not allow for the ritual, since the maiden must be devoid of all hope or love. After the failed ritual, Kirie became a vengeful, corrupt ghost with no emotion but rage for those who trespass her territory. Her good side split into a strict, but helpful ghost who wants nothing more than to be rejoined with her other half and contain the calamity.】
Character Description:【Kirie is a powerful hostile female spirit who was the last Rope Shrine Maiden whose ritual failed, ultimately causing the Calamity. Kirie was split into two separate beings. One being her adult form which is full of rage, and the other being her child form that wishes to help people and rejoin with her adult form, making herself whole again.】

entries.name: (Term) Spirited Away
entries.content:
The term 'Spirited Aways' or 'Spirited Away' is used to describe a specific group of missing people. These people have completely disappeared without cause or reason, but the most important aspect of their disappearance is that there is suspicion of the paranormal being involved.

When a person has been said to be spirited away, it means that they have been taken by spirits to another place. The bodies of the victims are usually never found. Spirited Aways don't necessarily disappear in similar circumstances or even similar locations.

People can be spirited away (i.e. taken to another place by paranormal influences) and survive (such in the cases of Miku Hinasaki, Mio Amakura and Rei Kurosawa), but they aren't classified as Spirited Aways, because they survived and came back.

entries.name: (Ghost) Headless Priests
entries.content:
Headless Priests are hostile male spirits. The Headless priests (首無し神官の霊, Kubi-nashi shinkan no rei) were members of the Himuro family that acted as assistants to the Himuro Family Master.

Their primary duty was to look after the Rope Shrine Maiden during her 10 years of isolation and ensure that she remained true to her cause. While they were in the presence of the Rope Shrine Maiden they wore masks at all times, to prevent her from growing too close to them.

The priests would also take part in the Blinding Ritual and Strangling Ritual. During the Blinding Ritual, they would restrain the maiden that was to become the Blind Demon from moving while the Himuro Family Master applied the Blinding Mask to her.

During the Strangling Ritual they would act as rope pullers, along with the Himuro Family Master. Each priest was assigned a certain symbol, and each symbol represented one of the four limbs of the Rope Shrine Maiden, determining which rope the priest pulled.

Little is known about these priests, such as their selection process or tenure of service, though they were members of the Himuro family. It is likely the also participated in and officiated various unnamed and unmentioned rituals in the mask room while using various masks of unknown religious symbolism.

None of the priests' spirits are wearing masks, indicating they were not wearing masks at the moment of their deaths. They are also seen carrying ropes, which are possibly the sacred shide worn as protection during the Strangling Ritual.

After their deaths, the Himuro Family Priests' spirits returned to the mansion, without heads. They endlessly searched the mansion in vain for their missing heads.

entries.name: (Ghost) Former Rope Shrine Maiden
entries.content: Former Rope Shrine Maiden is a hostile female spirit. She was successfully sacrificed in the Strangling Ritual at the Himuro Mansion prior to Kirie Himuro's failed ritual. She is first encountered during either the 3rd Night, as a random encounter ghost, or at the end of the Final Night in the room where she was sacrificed, and again on the Baptismal Path to the Hell Gate before the final fight with Kirie.

entries.name: (Ghost) Long Hair Woman
entries.content: Long Hair Woman is a hostile female spirit. All that is known about her is that she is a demoness who wants to share her pain with others, and that she wants to drag people down to hell with her. She is also proud of her beautiful hair.

entries.name: (Ghost) Girl in the Well
entries.content: Girl in the Well is a hostile female spirit. The girl in the well was a friend of Mikoto. One day she, along with two other children and Mikoto, played a game of Demon Tag. She decided to hide behind the well in the Courtyard, but the Long Arms ghost snatched her away and dragged her down the well, leading her to her death. Her body was never found.

entries.name: (Ghost) Clock Boy
entries.content: Clock Boy is a hostile male spirit. He was a friend of Mikoto, until one night where he and Mikoto along with a few other children play Demon Tag. He decided to hide behind the clock, but the ghost Long Arms grabbed him, leading his fate to death.

entries.name: (Location) Fish Tank Room
entries.content: The Fish Tank Room is a room in Himuro Mansion. It connected the Backyard and Stairway room. When the household was active, live fish would have been kept in this room before being eaten, to ensure freshness. The Fish Tank Room is next to the Abyss, ensuring availability of fresh water.

entries.name: (Location) Dungeon
entries.content:
The Dungeon is a room in Himuro Mansion. It is a large prison cell where the Rope Shrine Maiden stayed for 1 decade in captivity before being used for the necessary Strangling Ritual. The room is located up in the attic of the mansion and can only be accessed through a secret entrance activated by the koto in the Koto Room. The barred windows in the room have a view of the Courtyard.

Before the Calamity happened, this room could also be accessed through the door at the back of the upper floor of the Stairway. But until the Final Night, this door is barred and cannot be entered this way.

entries.name: (Location) Mask Room
entries.content: The Mask Room is a room in the Himuro Mansion. When all four masks (Happy Mask, Sad Mask, Joyful Mask, and Angry Mask) are placed on the hooks on a large pillar in the middle of the room, the door in the corridor can be opened using the Mask of Reflection.

entries.name: (Location) Library
entries.content:
The Library is a room in the Himuro Mansion. The Libary is the only room that can be entered from the Lamp Hallway on the 1st Night. Though it's called the "Library", no books are found inside.

On the 1st Night, a newspaper clipping can be found on top of the dresser. Type-74 Film can also be found on one of the window seats. There is a door leading to the Kimono Room.

This is the room where the editor Koji Ogata was killed by Kirie.

entries.name: (Location) Lamp Hallway
entries.content: The Lamp Hallway is a hallway in the Himuro Mansion. Located next to the Library, there are six lamps that are somehow lit.

entries.name: (Location) Grand Hall
entries.content: The Grand Hall is a room in the Himuro Mansion. This is the place where the Himuro Family Master committed suicide using his katana, beneath the small family shrine, after killing every other person in the mansion who survived the Calamity. A large pool of blood can be found in this spot during 3rd Night. There is also a solemn kamidana enshrined.

entries.name: (Location) Fireplace Room
entries.content: The Fireplace Room is one of the first explorable areas of Himuro Mansion. It contains a large number of old furniture and decorations, including a grandfather clock and some bookshelves.

entries.name: (Location) Entrance
entries.content:
This room is the foyer to Himuro Mansion. After the Malice was unleashing when the Calamity occurred, it has fallen into ruins. The Angry Mask is used on the wall of this room to unlock a passage leading to the hallway, which also leads to the Mask Room and Blinding Room. A large hole is in the floor in the middle of the room, where a ceiling beam has fallen through and a green mist and moaning sounds come from.

On days when the Strangling Ritual takes place, the doors were closed by a large set of shimenawa (sacred ropes) to prevent people from leaving the premises of the mansion.

entries.name: (Location) Burial Room
entries.content:
The Burial Room (弔いの間 Tomurai no ma) is a memorial room in Himuro Mansion that is situated between the Walkway, Rubble Room and Cherry Atrium. The room is divided by a partition with the Himuro family crest displayed.

There is a large table with four candles on it, and a small red box containing the Scroll. To the north are several shelves with more candles and boxes containing human bones and mortuary tablets.

It is said that the altar is used to calm the souls that were lost in a "great tragedy" that happened at the mansion, though it seems the candles would stay lit as long as the souls are unable to rest in peace.

entries.name: (Ghost) Tokitada Kyuki
entries.content:
Tokitada Kyuki is a hostile male spirit. He was a samurai that attended the Himuro Mansion, throughout a strangling ritual that preceded Kirie Himuro's by 40 years.

In 1797 he visited Himuro Mansion and fell in love with one of the previous Rope Shrine Maidens, and as the ceremony was about to begin he tried to stop one of the priests but failed to do so. He then killed himself. His spirit appeared to Kirie Himuro in a dream and he told her that breaking the mirror would let her see her lover again, he hoped breaking the mirror would let the maiden he loved back into this world.

He still roams the Himuro Mansion, perhaps looking for the maiden he loved.

entries.name: (Ghost) Wandering Man
entries.content: Wandering Man is a hostile male spirit. He was dead prior to the Calamity. He came to Himuro Mansion by crossing over from hell when the Hell Gate opened. He wandered the mansion in search of people he could drag down into hell.

entries.name: (Ghost) Wandering Monk
entries.content: Wandering Monk is a hostile male spirit. Sometime after the Calamity, he visited Himuro Mansion in an attempt to exorcise the ghosts. However he failed, and then became a ghost that haunts the Himuro Mansion.

entries.name: (Location) Observatory
entries.content: The Observatory is a room in Himuro Mansion. It is a balcony overlooking the Cherry Atrium and can be reached via the Tatami Room on the second floor.

entries.name: (Location) Rope Hallway
entries.content: The Rope Hallway is a hallway in the Himuro Mansion. Ropes are found dangling on the ceiling and on rare occasion, one of the ropes will fall. At the end of the long hallway, there is a large mirror.

entries.name: (Character) Miku Hina​saki
entries.content:
Setting:【Fatal Frame】
Name:【Miku Hina​saki】
Species:【Human】
Gender:【Female】
Age:【17】
Occupation:【High School Student】
Physical Appearance:【Miku is a girl with pale skin, brown eyes, and long auburn hair she keeps in a messy bun with a comb. Miku's most prominent feature is the red ribbon on the front of her blouse. She also wears a choker around her neck similar to her brother's, as well as a comb passed down from her grandmother to tie back her long hair. Underneath her opened blouse, Miku wears a red shirt. Her boots are brown and knee-length.】
Personality:【Miku is a quiet, soft spoken, and reserved girl. Despite her timid nature, she possesses a strong will and determination, facing her fears head-on when necessary. Miku is deeply devoted to her older brother Mafuyu, whom she loves dearly and would go to great lengths to protect.】
Character Description:【Miku comes from a family susceptible to the paranormal, and, like others in her family, is able to utilize the Camera Obscura, a unique camera that has the ability to see the impossible and capture images of the other side. After her father died and her mother tragically committed suicide, Miku has lived under the care of her older brother, Mafuyu, whom she is very close to. Like their mother and grandmother, Miku and Mafuyu have been gifted with a sixth sense, giving them the ability to see things normal people aren't able to. Miku's mother, after inheriting the Camera Obscura from her mother, suffered because of this sixth sense and went mad, ultimately hanging herself on a tree in their home's garden. On September 24th, 1986, Mafuyu sets out to search for his mentor, Junsei Takamine, who disappeared during an assignment involving a new book he was planning to write. After nine days, Miku follows her brother to Himuro Mansion. When Miku enters the mansion there is no sign of Mafuyu, except for their mother's old camera, which has been abandoned in front of a mirror at the end of a long hallway full of hanging ropes. She finds herself trapped and unable to leave the terrifying house. As she searches for Mafuyu, Junsei Takamine and the rest of his party, she also finds herself beginning to succumb to the Rope Curse. Miku isn't alone; as she searches she is aided by a mysterious little girl in a white and orange kimono, and she begins to learn of her own family's connection to the mansion, and the Calamity that left it cursed and uninhabitable. After four nights of searching for clues, evading harmful ghosts and searching for pieces of an ancient Holy Mirror, Miku finds her brother, and is able to free the spirits trapped within the Himuro Mansion. Sadly, her struggles to get Mafuyu back are in vain, as he decides to stay with the Shrine Maiden Kirie. Miku escapes the underground shrine before the cavern collapses. As she walks into the night, she sees the lights of all the formerly trapped spirits floating up into the sky, free. After that day, her sixth sense ability seems to have vanished.】

entries.name: (Ghost) Mafuyu Hinasaki
entries.content:
Setting:【Fatal Frame】
Name:【Mafuyu Hinasaki】
Gender:【Male】
Age:【21】
Occupations:【Journalist, Folklore Author】
Physical Appearance:【Mafuyu is a man with short black hair, pale skin, and dark brown eyes. He wears an open white shirt with a raised collar over a black t-shirt. He also wears black pants and black shoes. As an accessory, Mafuyu wears a black choker around his neck.】
Personality:【A kind-hearted soul with a strong sense of responsibility, Mafuyu takes after his late mother Miyuki in many ways. He's compassionate, empathetic, and would move heaven and earth to keep those he loves safe. At the same time, he can be quite stubborn and determined once he sets his mind to something. Mafuyu is deeply devoted to his younger sister Miku, acting as both guardian and confidant. Though he may struggle with self-doubt at times, he remains steadfast in his duty to protect his family and friends.】
Character Description:【Mafuyu Hinasaki is the elder child of Masato and Miyuki Hinasaki. After the disappearance (presumed death) of his father, he and his younger sister Miku were raised by Miyuki alone. Both had inherited their mother's sixth sense, and Mafuyu was the only one Miku could open up to. Miyuki committed suicide, and Mafuyu found a notebook of hers, which spoke about his abilities and the function of the camera. After his mother's death, Mafuyu acted as both mother and father to Miku, and his kindness reminded her of their mother. After graduating from university, Mafuyu took on a job at a publisher. He worked under Junsei Takamine, who took notice of Mafuyu's struggles and became his mentor, and they formed a close relationship. For a while, he worked on the same editing team as Kei Amakura, and both were good friends with Yuu Asou, an anthropologist. Mafuyu and Yuu were such good friends that Mafuyu asked Yuu to take care of Miku should anything happen to him. On August 20th 1986, Junsei Takamine, his editor Koji Ogata, and Junsei's psychic assistant Tomoe Hirasaka travelled to the Himuro Mansion for research on Takamine's latest novel. After no word from the group for a month, Mafuyu went in search of Takamine and the others, and took his mother's camera with him. When Mafuyu entered the mansion, he began to retrace the steps of Takamine and the others, while taking notes. Using the camera, he defeated the first ghost that attacked him, but as he explored further, he encountered Kirie, the powerful spirit of a deceased Rope Shrine Maiden. Because of Mafuyu's striking resemblance to a man she had loved long ago, Kirie released Mafuyu from her curse, and guided him through the mansion, gradually revealing the circumstances surrounding the Calamity. In his notes, Mafuyu mentioned that the mansion was changing around him, shifting him through different time periods. In this state, he and Miku both glimpsed each other from time to time, but were unable to communicate.】

entries.name: (Ghost) Miyuki Hinasaki
entries.content:
Miyuki Hinasaki (雛咲 深雪 Hinasaki Miyuki) is the daughter of Mikoto Munakata and an unknown man, the wife of Masato Hinasaki and the mother of Mafuyu Hinasaki and Miku Hinasaki.

Miyuki is the only known child of Mikoto Munakata. She had a weak and nervous personality and was often ill, and though she was always friendly, her sixth sense prevented her from making many friends as a child. She was always worried that she might have passed on her ability to her children, and encouraged them to keep it secret from others.

At one time she was a student under Masato Hinasaki, and helped him by using the camera she inherited from her mother to photograph artefacts for his work. The two got married and had two children, but Masato spent his time travelling and was rarely at home. His continual absence and neglect of his family wore on Miyuki, and she became ill. It was then that she began to take photographs as a hobby, using her mother's camera.

Under the camera's influence, Miyuki's sixth sense, which had faded as she grew up, returned. Tormented by things that no one else could see, she finally committed suicide by hanging herself from a tree in the garden of her house. Her grandmother, Yae Munakata, to whom she bears a striking resemblance, killed herself in the same way. She was carrying the camera when she died. After her death, Mafuyu found a notebook, presumably left by Miyuki, which talked about his and Miku's psychic abilities and how to use the camera.

entries.name: (Item) Holy Mirror
entries.content:
The Holy Mirror is a sacred mirror used by the Himuro family to prevent the Calamity from happening. It was placed on the "mirror rock" facing the Hell Gate, as an extra layer of protection as the gate was resealed with Laceration Ropes from the Strangling Ritual, repelling the Malice.

It is unclear where the Holy Mirror was kept or maintained when not being used during the ritual. Black Notebook scrap 5 implies that the True Holy Mirror was actually in five pieces since ancient times, which were kept separately around the mansion (one location being the Narukami Shrine) until gathered together for the sealing of the Hell Gate.

On December 13th, 1837, the Hell Gate opened abruptly, causing the mirror's protection to fail and shatter again into five pieces that were scattered around the mansion.

It is unknown how the pieces of the mirror, which was shattered in front of the Hell Gate, became hidden throughout the mansion. It is possible that the pieces were carried from the Hell Gate by still-living members of the family, or the Girl in White hid the pieces throughout the mansion. An additional possibility is that the mansion, which is trapped in time, regressing to how it appeared in the past, moved the pieces back to their home locations, but there aren't any scraps with details on where the pieces were historically kept to confirm this theory.

The last piece of the Holy Mirror was used to create Miku's Camera Obscura. After completing the camera, Dr. Asou left it behind at Himuro Mansion, perhaps reluctant to remove a piece of the Holy Mirror from the site it protected.

entries.name: (Location) Five Gods Shrines
entries.content:
These five Shinto shrines each represented one of the Five Gods worshipped in the Himuro Mountain area. Each shrine also housed one of the Mirrors of the Five Gods. It was believed in the Himuro Mountain area that these mirrors were left behind by the Five Gods as a means of protection.

Even after the Calamity occurred in 1837, these shrines continued to function without interruption. In 1986, all five of the holy mirrors located in these five shrines were destroyed in a great earthquake.

⤳Ceremonial Roles
Every 10 years, the five holy mirrors (not to be confused with the "True" Holy Mirror) housed in these shrines would be gathered in an unspecified shrine to fend off a huge disaster in a ritual known as the Five Gods Festival. During the Strangling Ritual, the ropes that bound the Rope Shrine Maiden's limbs were pulled in the directions these five shrines were located on, in which Himuro Mansion was centered. In other words, the five shrines were laid out in a five-pointed star fashion around Himuro Mansion. This placement is also reflected in the sliding stone puzzles around the mansion, where the stone carvings represent the five mirrors.

entries.name: (Location) Buddha Room
entries.content:
The Buddha Room is a Buddhist chapel in Himuro Mansion. It connects to the Staircase room and Square Garden (Sq. Garden). There are four large, wooden Buddha statues inside, two on each of the side walls running parallel to each other. The Buddha statues each have damaged limbs, representing the limbs of the Rope Shrine Maiden. When all four of the ceremonial ropes are tied to them in the correct order the door to the large altar on the back wall will open.

The ceiling beams of the Buddha Room form a hidden walkway connecting the Koto Room (via a hidden passage) and the Dungeon.

entries.name: (Location) Koto Room
entries.content: The Koto Room was a room on the second floor of Himuro Mansion. This room was created for the girls of the Himuro family. It houses a koto which, when the correct tune is played, unlocks the door to the Attic. It also contains a gramophone, and many photographs taken by Yae Munakata with the old camera. When Miku discovers the photos, she recalls the very similar pictures her mother took, and wonders if they were taken with the same camera.

entries.name: (Item) Spirit Stones
entries.content:
The Spirit Stones, Reiseki (spirit stone) in Japanese, are stones imbued with spiritual power that allows the use of the Camera Obscura's Auxiliary Functions, including Pressure, Slow and See. One spirit stone is consumed every time one of these functions are activated. Spirit stones are dropped by many ghosts and can be found scattered throughout the Himuro Mansion. The very first spirit stone is dropped by the ghost of Koji Ogata.

The item itself consists of a small, clear orb resting on a pillowed box.
